title: Pan Am 1104
summary: Pan Am Flight V-1104, a Martin M-130 flying boat, crashed into mountainous terrain near Ukiah, California during descent. Deteriorating weather with heavy rain, strong winds, thick cloud cover and fog forced the captain to descend to a lower altitude. The aircraft, far off course in poor visibility, struck a mountain at about 2500 feet while descending at an angle of 10°. All 19 people on board were killed.

factors.evidence: Heavy rain, strong winds, thick cloud cover, and fog forced the captain to descend to a lower altitude.
The far-off-course aircraft crashed into a mountain, indicating loss of positional awareness.
The aircraft crashed into a mountain at about 2500 ft, descending at an angle of 10°, whereupon it clipped a number of trees before crashing, breaking up, and burning.

events.text: Flight V-1104 departed from Pearl Harbor on Oahu at 5:30 pm on January 20, 1943.
On the morning of January 21, 1943, the aircraft ran into poor weather as it flew north over California towards San Francisco.
Heavy rain, strong winds, thick cloud cover, and fog forced the captain to descend to a lower altitude.
The aircraft crashed into a mountain at about 2500 ft, descending at an angle of 10°, and clipped trees before crashing, breaking up, and burning.

title: Lady Be Good
summary: B-24D Liberator Lady Be Good, a new aircraft with a first-time crew on their first combat mission, bombed Naples on April 4, 1943. On return, a sandstorm caused the crew to overshoot their air base at Soluch in Libya. The crew failed to realize they had overflown the base in the sandstorm and continued flying south into the Libyan Desert for many hours. When fuel was exhausted, eight of the nine crew members bailed out successfully. The survivors walked in the desert for eight days with only a single canteen of water to share, believing they were close to the Mediterranean coast. All nine crew members ultimately died.
probable_cause: The first-time crew failed to realize they had overflown their air base in a sandstorm. After continuing to fly south into the desert for many hours, the crew bailed out when the plane's fuel was exhausted. The survivors then died in the desert trying to walk to safety, unaware they were 400 miles inland.

factors.evidence: A sandstorm caused eight B-24s to return to Soluch, leaving only four aircraft to continue the operation including Lady Be Good.
The crew failed to realize they had overflown their air base at Soluch in a sandstorm and continued flying south into the Libyan Desert for many hours.
Lady Be Good's crew were also new, having only arrived in Libya a week before on March 18, and they flew their first mission together on April 4.

A diary recovered from co-pilot Robert Toner indicated that none of the men were aware they had been flying over land when they bailed out, or that they were 400 miles inland. It has been speculated the dark empty desert floor may have resembled open sea.
After flying 440 miles into the desert, the plane's fuel was exhausted and the crew bailed out.

title: BOAC 777
summary: The Douglas DC-3 departed Lisbon for Bristol on 1 June 1943 and was attacked by eight German Junkers Ju 88 fighter aircraft approximately 200 miles northwest of the Spanish coast. The aircraft crashed into the Bay of Biscay with all 17 occupants killed, including actor Leslie Howard and several British passengers believed to be spies. German motivations for the attack remain unclear, though one theory suggests they believed British Prime Minister Winston Churchill was aboard.
probable_cause: The aircraft was attacked by eight German Junkers Ju 88 fighter planes. The attack occurred during an intensification of air combat over the Bay of Biscay in 1943, though the specific reason for targeting this aircraft remains undetermined.

title: Bakers Creek air crash
summary: Boeing B-17C took off from Mackay Airfield in foggy conditions on 14 June 1943 headed for Port Moresby. Flames were observed along the fuselage and wings shortly after takeoff. The aircraft made a low-altitude turn and crashed near Bakers Creek, Queensland, killing 40 of 41 people aboard. The cause of the crash remains undetermined.

title: American Airlines 63 (Flagship Ohio)
summary: Flight 63 cruised at 2,000-2,500 ft on the Louisville-Nashville leg when thunderstorms around Smiths Grove produced extreme turbulence and strong downdrafts that forced the aircraft to lose altitude. The DC-3 descended until it struck trees, then slid across an open field. Two passengers survived; all four crew members perished.
probable_cause: The extreme turbulence and conditions caused by the nearby thunderstorm created such severe flying conditions that the pilot was unable to maintain control of the aircraft.
